talk_track: Most of my work now is one transition: an AI offering outgrowing the platform and the org that was built for the older product. Your open CTO posting for AddSearch describes it as "a company at an inflection point: maintaining a stable, high-SLA enterprise product while scaling a newer AI/RAG solution." With five engineers and one solutions engineer, that is two operating models sharing one on-call rotation — enterprise SLAs punish change, RAG demands it constantly. The quiet failure mode isn't a bad hire; it's the RAG line borrowing reliability capacity from your contract customers until an SLA breach picks the tradeoff for you. I ran both clocks at Ripple and Tricentis: GitOps delivery for the fast side, error budgets and AI-assisted incident response for the SLA side, MTTR down about 40%. Who's holding the SLA side while the CTO search runs? — Daniel Kirichanski
